items.stem:
This question concerns the region R between y = 4x and y = x².
(a) Find the coordinates of the points of intersection of y = 4x and y = x².
(b) Find the exact area of the region R between the curves.
(c) Find the exact volume generated when R is rotated through 2π about the x-axis.
(d) Explain why the volume is not π∫(y₁ − y₂)² dx.
(e) Find the exact volume generated when R is rotated through 2π about the y-axis.
items.answer: (a) (0, 0), (4, 16) (b) 32/3 (c) 2048π/15 (d) each cross-section is an annulus of area π(y₁² − y₂²) (e) 128π/3
items.markingKey: (a) equate (M1) A1 A1 (b) ∫ from 0 to 4 of (4x − (x²)) dx (M1) A1 (c) washer π∫(y₁² − y₂²) dx (M1) A1 A1 (d) R1 (e) x in terms of y for each curve (M1); π∫(x_outer² − x_inner²) dy (M1) A1 [Total 12 marks]

items.stem:

items.stem: Explain how to find the volume generated by rotating the region between two curves about the x-axis.
items.answer: Subtract the inner volume from the outer: π∫(y_outer² − y_inner²) dx, which is not π∫(y_outer − y_inner)² dx.

Consider I = ∫ sin³x dx.
(a) Write sin³x in terms of sin x and cos x so that the substitution u = cos x can be used.
(b) Hence find ∫ sin³x dx.
(c) Find the exact value of ∫ from 0 to π/2 of sin³x dx.

items.answer: (a) sin x (1 − cos²x) (b) cos(x)³/3 − cos(x) + C (c) 2/3 (d) keep one sin x, convert the rest using sin²x = 1 − cos²x, then u = cos x
